title: The Vasoactive Potential of Kisspeptin-10 in the Peripheral Vasculature

what_it_measured.text: Here, we investigated the potential of Kp-10, the shortest biologically active kisspeptin, to influence microvascular effects, concentrating on the cutaneous vasculature.

dose.text: Female CD1 mice were anaesthetised, injected with Evans Blue dye i.v. and treated intradermally in the dorsal skin with 0.3–10nmol kisspeptin-10 (KP), 300pmol substance P (SP) or saline control (Veh) for 30 minutes.

route.text: Female CD1 mice were anaesthetised, injected with Evans Blue dye i.v. and treated intradermally in the dorsal skin with 0.3–10nmol kisspeptin-10 (KP), 300pmol substance P (SP) or saline control (Veh) for 30 minutes.

endpoint.text: Therefore, changes in dorsal skin blood flow were assessed by clearance of intradermally injected 99mtechnetium.
Kp-10 caused a dose-dependent increase in oedema formation (0.3–10nmol/injection site), assessed by Evans Blue albumin dye extravasation, in the dorsal skin of CD1 mice.
In order to possibly learn more of the potential of Kp-10 to influence cardiovascular dysfunction, gene expression was evaluated in different tissues collected from hypertensive animals.

reported_results.text: Results are expressed as copy number and normalised by comparison to reference genes HPRT-1, SDHA and PLA2 using GeNorm version 3.4.
However, 10nmol/ site Kp-10 induced vasoconstriction was significantly reduced (p≤0.05), but not totally inhibited, by co-treatment with indomethacin.
However, at 10 nmol/site Kp-10 caused a significant decrease in blood flow from 3 nmol/site suggesting vasoconstrictor activity in the peripheral vasculature (p≤0.05).
Endothelin , an established vasoconstrictor agent [28], endothelin-1 caused a significant decrease in clearance from the injection site (60% decrease from vehicle at a dose of 30pmol, p≤0.01.
In this case, hypertensive animals exhibited systolic pressure readings of 129±3.8mmHg compared to controls (118±0.99mmHg).
Saline vehicle was adjusted to 100% and results displayed as a % change to controls.
